title: Coral and the Ember
premise: Casper Eriksen has survived by silence, speaking with beasts only in secret and guiding smugglers through the Thornfell passes. When the crown's witch-hunters burn a neighboring village, Casper flees into the deep mountains and discovers the truth: the king is bound to an ancient ember-spirit that feeds on the gifts of people like them, devouring magic to sustain its stolen throne. Guided by a dying wolf-mother and an exiled hunt-captain who once served the crown, Casper journeys to the capital to unbind the king before the ember consumes every gifted soul in the realm. In the end, Casper breaks the binding at terrible cost—the wolf-mother dies, the captain is maimed—and the freed, broken king must answer for his years of complicity, leaving justice delivered outside any court.
about_author: Casper Winterbourne is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in wild places, exploring how ordinary people survive systems built to destroy them.

chapters.title: The Quiet Roads
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper guides a smuggler's caravan through the Thornfells, trading quiet words with ravens and mountain goats while hiding their gift from the crew. The chapter establishes their careful, invisible life and the warmth they find in animal company. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness—the sense that a life half-hidden is only half-lived.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The caravan reaches Lowmark village and finds it burned, a royal proclamation nailed to the well: all beast-speakers to be surrendered or slain. A survivor's dying dog tells Casper who came—crown hunters in black-and-gold. Casper flees alone into the high passes as the caravan scatters. Emotional beat: terror and guilt, the shattering of the belief that invisibility was safety.

chapters.title: The Wolf-Mother
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Starving in the deep winter fells, Casper is found by Vaela, an ancient wolf who speaks with startling clarity. She reveals the ember: a spirit bound beneath the capital that devours gifted bloodlines, and that the king has been its vessel for thirty years. She offers to guide Casper if they will carry her message to the city. Emotional beat: reluctant hope—a purpose larger than survival.

chapters.title: A Hunter's Oath
chapters.summary: POV: Sera Vance (the hunt-captain). Sera, the crown's most feared gift-hunter, interrogates a captured speaker and realizes the king's edicts serve no law she swore to protect. Her own sister was taken years ago; the records don't add up. She burns her commission and deserts, heading for the Thornfells. Emotional beat: disillusionment curdling into resolve—justice requires breaking the law.

chapters.title: Thieves' Gate
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Descending from the mountains, Casper is ambushed by bounty men but saved by Sera, who recognizes what Casper is and chooses alliance over arrest. Uneasy, they travel together toward the capital, trading truths by firelight. Vaela shadows them from the ridgelines. Emotional beat: brittle trust between natural enemies, warming into something like respect.

chapters.title: The Gilded Rot
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Inside the capital, they find a city of informants and ash-marked doorways where the gifted have been quietly harvested for decades. A contact in the underworld reveals the binding ritual happens at the solstice eclipse—nine days away—and that the king himself sometimes begs strangers for help before the ember silences him. Emotional beat: dread and urgency; the scale of the corruption dwarfs anything Casper imagined.

chapters.title: What the King Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Using her old credentials, Sera infiltrates the palace and reaches the king during his rare lucid hour. He confirms everything: he bargained with the ember to win a war, and it has worn him ever since, growing stronger with each gifted soul consumed. He gives her the binding's true name—but the palace guards take him back, and Sera barely escapes. Emotional beat: horror and pity; the tyrant is also a prisoner.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Undercity
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Their underworld contact sells them out for amnesty; hunters corner Casper and Sera in the flooded catacombs. Vaela arrives and tears through the hunters, but is gravely wounded, and Sera loses her sword arm holding the escape route. They reach the ritual chamber's threshold with hours left, carrying their dying allies. Emotional beat: grief and fury—the price of the fight made flesh.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At the eclipse, Casper enters the ember's mindscape using their gift, finds the king's buried self, and speaks him free while Vaela, dying, holds the spirit's attention with her last strength. Casper offers the ember not a soul but its freedom, unmaking the bargain rather than replacing it. The spirit dissolves; the binding shatters across the realm, and every hidden gifted person feels their chains fall away. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into liberation.

chapters.title: Emberless
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The king, freed but broken, publicly confesses and abdicates to face judgment outside the crown's protection—no court, only the people he wronged. Sera, one-armed, takes charge of rebuilding; Vaela is buried on a high ridge. Casper walks home through the Thornfells, no longer hiding, beasts calling greetings from every slope. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—survival was never free, but it was worth its price.
